Oral Order 08 / Dated : 19.01.2023
1.

The instant criminal misc. petition has been filed for quashing the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Lower Bazar P.S. Case 55 of 2018 (G.R. No. 946 of 2018) including the order taking cognizance dated 04.02.2020 under Sections 498A, 406, 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. Petitioner nos. 1 and 2 are the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the complainant-informant in the complaint which has been filed under Sections 498A, 406, 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The main allegation against the petitioners is that the complainant's father has transferred Rs.14 Lakh through bank and Rs.10 Lakh in cash for fulfilling the demand of the accused persons.
There is further allegation that 4 to 5 days after marriage the demand was raised by these petitioners from the complainant.
It is also alleged that 15 Tola of Gold was misappropriated by petitioner no. 2.
The complaint petition was forwarded by the learned Magistrate under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. for investigation.

After investigation, the case has been found to be true and charge sheet has been submitted and thereafter cognizance has been taken under Sections 498A, 406, 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that while forwarding the complaint for registration of the case and investigation, the mandate of law as laid down on (2015) 6 SCC 287 (Priyanka Srivastava and Anr. Vs. State of U.P. & Ors.) has not been followed.

entities.text: (2015) 6 SCC 287 (Priyanka Srivastava and Anr. Vs. State of U.P. & Ors.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relying on paras 30 and 31 of the said judgment, it has been submitted that there are three requirements to be satisfied before a complaint is preferred under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.

Firstly, there has to be prior application of Section 154(1) and 154(3) Cr.P.C. while filing the petitioner under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
Secondly, the affidavit should be sworn in support of the complaint petition seeking investigation and lastly, there should be application of judicial mind while passing such order.
4.
It is submitted that none of these conditions has been satisfied by the court below.
Further whatever allegation is there, that are regarding the incident that took place before the marriage and there is no allegation after the marriage to make the offence under Section 498A of IPC.
The petitioners are not sharing the domestic household with the complainant.
5. It is submitted on behalf of the complainant-informant that Rs.14 Lakh has been transferred by the Bank transaction which is unimpeachable evidence on demand of dowry.
There are allegations of further demand and the police on investigation has found the case to be true.
With regard to the question on affidavit, it is submitted that the complaint petition has not been filed with a prayer for forwarding the matter for investigation under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
However, in para 27 of the complaint petition there is specific reference that the concerned police station refused to receive the complaint constrained by which the complainant moved the court.
This is not a fit case for quashing of the cognizance.
The instant Cr. Misc. Petition stands dismissed.
